ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized representatives against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Canadian Criminal Code terrorist entities list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, FINTRAC's recognized lists, and any OFAC-specific watchlists adopted by Canadian financial institutions. The procedure must include at least one automated engine or registered migration service and a manual review by a designated compliance officer. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), persons from sanctioned jurisdictions, or where wire transfers exceed C$10,000. Canada's Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Client Due Diligence requirements are enforced under PCMLTFA regulations and may be audited by FINTRAC. The partnership must maintain ongoing monitoring and update screening at every material change in ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) / Alberta Corporate Registry online name search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be in English or French, but Alberta specifically uses English as primary filing language. Non-Latin alphabet names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet and the transliteration will constitute the official registered name. The legal element must appear in English (e.g., 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'LP') or French (e.g., 'Société en commandite', 'S.E.C.'). Names must not be identical, confusingly similar, or likely to deceive; must comply with Alberta's business name regulation under the Partnership Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected by Alberta Corporate Registry, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal and application to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of rejection. The appeal must include: (1) a completed 'Name Request/Appeal' form, (2) a NUANS name search report, (3) a detailed explanation of why the name is not confusing with or prohibited from existing entries, (4) written consents or trademark registrations as applicable, and (5) supporting origin or invented word evidence. Appeals are reviewed by the Corporate Registry's name advisory committee. If the appeal is denied, a further judicial review may be sought in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act. Name reservations are non-extendable except by providing a new NUANS search or, in case of pending trademark opposition, a statutory written extension request reviewed on discretionary grounds; the maximum extension period is 30 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable in principle for a hyper-casual mobile game publishing limited partnership provided that the registered office is a physical street address in Alberta, service of process can be physically accepted, business hours are maintained, and mail is not merely forwarded to a P.O. box. A virtual office or registered agent service is permissible where the provider maintains a physical Alberta street address, accepts service on behalf of the partnership, and complies with the Partnership Act requirements for registered office. The requirement remains that all records and minute books must be available in Alberta or accessible immediately from the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% annual likelihood of unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk digital advertising and publishing entity. Physical inspections may be higher if the partnership claims Alberta R&D tax credits or applies for government grants, or if registry compliance flags are raised. Alberta Registries may conduct periodic validation checks of registered offices and registered agents, and FINTRAC may perform AML compliance inspections. Expected probability is 5-10% per year for this industry and structure.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies / Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration of Limited Partnership (Form RC-1) together with executed partnership agreement; Certificate of Limited Partnership issued by the Registrar upon completion
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an Alberta limited partnership. Contributions may be in cash, property, or services as agreed in the partnership agreement; no escrow or capital verification account is required under Alberta law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of the General Partner of the Limited Partnership hereby accepts the subscription for partnership interests by the initial Limited Partner for the capital contribution set out in the partnership agreement; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Limited Partnership is adopted and fixed at the address set out in the Registration of Limited Partnership; RESOLVED, that the appointment of the initial officers of the General Partner and the authorized signatories of the Limited Partnership be and is hereby ratified. step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via OneLink (Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed limited partnership name to ensure no conflict with existing registered names. If the name is available, reserve it for 90 days by filing the name reservation online or by paper, paying the prescribed fee. The reserved name will be used for the Registration of Limited Partnership.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts with an existing mark, file an alternate name reservation or apply for a consent letter from the owner of the conflicting name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, OneLink portal or mail to: Corporate Registry, 7th Floor, 10025 106 Street, Edmonton, AB T5J 1G7
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form RC-1 (Registration of Limited Partnership) including registered office address, general partner and limited partner information, contribution schedule, and the signed consent of the registered office. Attach the NUANS reservation or name search report. File via OneLink or in-person/mail. The Registrar reviews for statutory compliance and issues a Certificate of Limited Partnership.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (not filed but retained by partners)
Registered office address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application, correct the specified defects or provide a written explanation within 30 days; re-file the amended Form RC-1 without additional fee if submitted in response to the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Limited Partnership and Corporate Registry Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant monitors the OneLink account or mailed certificate. Verify that the registered details (legal name, partners, registered office) exactly match the intended structure. Download or request a printable Corporate Registry Extract for banking, tax, and counterparty due diligence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of clerical errors under the Corporate Registry Act by filing a Statement of Correction; if the certificate data is wrong, amend the registration by filing a Statement of Amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Tax Account Numbers with Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online via CRA Business Registration or mail Form RC1 for the limited partnership. The LP will receive a Business Number (BN) and applicable program accounts, including GST/HST (for taxable supplies) and possibly payroll (if employees). Provide the Certificate of Limited Partnership and partnership agreement. Ensure the general partner's corporate information is consistent.
required_dossiers: Business Number of general partner (if already registered)
Form RC1 or online application reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or withholds a program account, call the CRA Business Enquiries line or submit a revised RC1; any delay in BN issuance is cured by using a temporary BN and filing the required return by deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial and Municipal Business Registration and Occupational Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (for provincial tax); Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta (WCB); applicable city business licence (e.g. Edmonton/Calgary) if physical office or home-based business
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Alberta Corporate Income Tax program (if applicable) and, if the LP or its general partner employs personnel in Alberta, register with WCB and obtain a WCB account. Should a physical office be opened, apply for a municipal business licence and occupational health/safety compliance. For a pure virtual gaming publisher with no office, only business licence may be required if business is conducted from a jurisdiction with mandatory licensing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contact the respective authority to rectify any registration deficiency; late registration penalties can be waived if the entity demonstrates a reasonable cause.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required for hyper-casual mobile game publishing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (not engaged)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No special fire safety or structural inspection beyond standard commercial tenancy obligations; maintains standard workplace safety and occupational health compliance for office staff if any.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - registration, assessment and collection of GST/HST, federal corporate income tax, and Alberta corporate income tax under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement; operational portals are Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca/business-taxes, My Business Account, and GST/HST NETFILE. Alberta-specific counterpart: Alberta Corporate Registry (alberta.ca/registries) issues the Limited Partnership Certificate of Registration, and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (ATRA) administers provincial tax statutes; Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax and no separate provincial VAT, so CRA remains the single indirect tax authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Alberta Limited Partnership at Alberta Corporate Registry - complete NUANS name search, file the Record of Limited Partnership, provide a registered address in Alberta, and appoint a resident registered agent; obtain the Alberta Corporate Access Number and Certificate of Registration. Step 2: Apply to CRA for the partnership's federal Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online or Form RC1, selecting the 'Partnership' legal type and requesting a GST/HST account (RT program) plus a payroll account if Canadian employees will be engaged; CRA issues a 15-character BN in the format 123456789 RT 0001. Step 3: If the LP is non-resident owned and controlled, CRA requires the representative partner to mail Form RC1 and Form RC871 to the International Tax Services Office; registration is mandatory once gross worldwide taxable supplies connected with Canada exceed C$30,000 in any four consecutive quarters. Step 4: Each non-resident partner must provide its foreign tax identification number and a certificate of residence for treaty purposes; CRA does not issue a separate partnership TIN beyond the BN. Step 5: After BN activation, the LP must file periodic GST/HST returns, a T5013 Partnership Information Return allocating income to partners, and the partners include Alberta corporate income tax on their T2 returns using the federal BN; no additional Alberta tax registration or provincial sales tax account is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - for Canadian income tax purposes the Alberta LP is fiscally transparent under Income Tax Act s.96: the partnership itself is not a taxpayer, computes income or loss at the partnership level, files the T5013 information return, and allocates income/loss to partners who are taxed in their own hands. Alberta does not impose entity-level income tax on the LP. For US federal income tax, the Canadian LP is a foreign eligible entity that defaults to partnership classification under Treas. Reg. sec. 301.7701-3(b)(2)(i)(B) when at least one general partner has unlimited liability, which is the standard structure. Territorial scope: Canadian-resident partners are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners are taxable in Canada only on Canadian-source business income and dispositions of taxable Canadian property allocated through the LP, subject to any income tax treaty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic 'check-the-box' classification election for partnerships. Available statutory elections and special-status mechanisms: (1) US federal Form 8832 check-the-box election under Treas. Reg. sec. 301.7701-3(c) to confirm or overturn the default partnership/association classification of the Canadian LP for US investors; (2) voluntary GST/HST registration election under ETA s.240(2.1), allowing the LP to register before crossing the C$30,000 compulsory threshold and to recover input tax credits and support export zero-rating; (3) ETA s.156 related-party election to treat qualifying non-arm's-length supplies between the LP and its corporate general partner as nil or fair-value consideration for GST purposes; (4) ITA s.96(8) partnership fiscal-period election permitting a non-calendar year-end where all partners' taxation years coincide; (5) hybrid mismatch treatment - Canada has not enacted BEPS Action 2 domestic hybrid legislation, so relief relies on the Canada-US Treaty Article IV(7) fiscally transparent entity clause and the Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test; no domestic hybrid election exists; (6) Alberta partnership legislation contains no tax classification election - fiscal effects flow solely from the ITA and ETA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under the Excise Tax Act, RSC 1985, c. E-15; in Alberta only the federal 5% GST applies, with no provincial sales tax or HST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 - a GST/HST registrant is required where taxable supplies made in Canada, including digital supplies and advertising inventory connected to Canada, exceed C$30,000 in any four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s.240(1)); non-resident persons carrying on business in Canada are subject to the same threshold; zero-rated export revenues count toward the threshold, so registration may be compulsory even when all game revenue originates offshore; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None - Canada has no mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or transaction-level API pre-clearance for GST/HST. Registrants must issue invoices containing the registration number, date, supplier name, taxable amount, and tax amount (ETA s.223) and must retain books and records in Canada or electronically accessible (ETA s.286). CRA has adopted a voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework based on Peppol PINT, but participation is optional. Filing occurs through GST/HST NETFILE or the GST Access API on a periodic return basis, not transaction-by-transaction clearance; the zero-rated export status is documented on the invoice as '0% GST'.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under ETA Schedule VI: (a) supplies of services made to a non-resident person (s.7) where the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada, not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, and not rendered to a person in Canada; (b) supplies of intangible property rights, including copyright and software licences, made to a non-resident (s.10) where the right is not for use predominantly in Canada; (c) exports of tangible goods (s.6). For the hyper-casual gaming model: (1) App Store and Google Play royalty/licence settlements - supplies of game IP and online-game rights to non-resident platform operators such as Apple Distribution International and Google Ireland Ltd. qualify for 0% under s.10 to the extent the platform's sublicence is not predominantly for use in Canada; (2) ad-network revenue - the supply of advertising inventory to non-resident ad-tech buyers such as AppLovin and AdMob/Google Ireland qualifies for 0% under s.7 where the contracted recipient is non-resident and the advertising is not directed at Canadian audiences; the Canadian-impression share must be treated as taxable at 5% unless marketplace or agency rules shift collection responsibility to the platform; (3) direct sales of digital game content to Canadian consumers are always taxable at 5% GST. Substantiation requires non-resident self-certification (W-8BEN-E or equivalent), contracts identifying the offshore recipient as principal, country-level download and impression reports demonstrating place of supply under ETA s.143.2, zero-rated invoices with recipient-country codes, and bank settlement records. No physical customs clearance applies to pure digital exports; there is no statutory FX repatriation deadline in Canada, the 180-day figure being a customary transfer-pricing documentation benchmark.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ETA s.286 books and records: zero-rated sales ledger with recipient-country jurisdiction codes and tax exemption indicator
Non-resident recipient evidence: W-8BEN-E, CRS self-certification, foreign tax identification number, or certificate of residence for each platform counterparty (Apple, Google, AppLovin, AdMob)
Executed distribution and monetization agreements: Apple Developer Program License Agreement, Google Play Distribution Agreement, AppLovin Publisher Agreement, and AdMob Terms
Foreign payout and FX records: AdMob and AppLovin settlement reports, bank SWIFT or inward remittance statements evidencing USD/EUR receipts from Ireland and US intermediaries
If physical goods are exported (promotional merchandise or gift cards): Canadian Export Reporting System B13A export declaration, bill of lading or waybill, and ETA Schedule VI s.6 export evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA export-verification audits focus on the recipient's non-resident status, the place of supply under ETA s.143.2, and whether digital services were in fact 'rendered to a person in Canada'. Where zero-rating is denied, CRA reassesses net GST, claws back input tax credits, and charges arrears interest at the prescribed rate compounded daily under ETA s.280. The gross-negligence penalty is the greater of C$250 and 25% of the net tax understated (ETA s.285). Misrepresentation, wilful default, or fraud extends the normal four-year reassessment window indefinitely under ETA s.298. Criminal tax evasion under ETA ss.326-327 carries fines of up to 200% of the amount sought to be evaded and imprisonment of up to five years. Late or misleading T5013 partnership filings attract separate administrative penalties. For US investors, parallel exposure includes IRC sec. 6662 accuracy-related penalties of 20-40% and potential subpart F or hybrid-transfer-pricing adjustments, making contemporaneous zero-rating documentation essential.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully convertible current account regime with unrestricted profit remittances for bona fide corporate operations. Capital account transactions are liberalized for routine equity injections and intercompany funding; prior approval from the Department of Finance is required only for portfolio investments exceeding CAD 100 million or certain real estate transactions. No surrender obligations apply to current account proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Exporters must submit periodic reports to Statistics Canada under the Export and Import Permits Act and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Funds may be freely converted through authorized foreign exchange dealers without statutory conversion ratios.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for cross-border payment facilitation via licensed fintech platforms (Wise, Revolut Business, Mercury) subject to FINTRAC registration and AML/CFT compliance. Electronic money institution licensing is not required for payment facilitation services; however, issuance of e-money or stored-value facilities requires authorization from the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital account opening is fully permitted for Alberta Limited Partnerships using FINTRAC-compliant e-KYC, video verification, and certified digital signatures. Physical presence is not mandatory for standard onboarding but may be required for high-value accounts or when beneficial ownership verification exceeds digital thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Limited Partnership, partnership agreement, ownership percentage schedule, and source-of-wealth affidavits

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border fund flows and trade purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade contracts, ad revenue invoices, payment processor statements, and board resolutions authorizing capital contributions
Commercial rationale memo, peer-reviewed gaming industry benchmarks, and independent audit confirmation

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose code 8897 (Capital Contribution) or 8899 (Equity Injection). All transactions require supporting documentation including Limited Partnership Agreement, board resolutions, and audited financial statements. FINTRAC suspicious transaction reporting thresholds apply; no prior approval needed for routine corporate funding below CAD 50,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements include SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers and issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banking networks. Game development disbursements and ad monetization payouts (AdMob, AppLovin) must reference specific trade contracts and be routed via licensed Canadian banks or authorized payment service providers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and applicable T5013 information slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Information slips are generally due within 3 months after the partnership fiscal period-end; the T5013 return is generally due within 5 months after the fiscal period-end. Filing is required when applicable under the Income Tax Act, including where specified partnership thresholds or partner-status conditions apply.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is generally CAD 25 per day, up to CAD 2,500, with additional assessment, interest, or information-demand consequences where applicable. No automatic Alberta LP strike-off is triggered solely by a late T5013 filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta limited partnership annual filing status review and event-driven registry updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Alberta limited partnerships generally have no recurring annual return or annual renewal filing. File amendments promptly when registered partnership information changes, including changes to the declaration of limited partnership, registered office, agent for service, or general partner information.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No annual filing delinquency penalty or automatic annual strike-off applies where no annual return is prescribed. Failure to update required registry information may impair legal notice, create administrative non-compliance, and result in applicable filing or enforcement consequences.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory independent-audit requirement or Alberta revenue/assets audit threshold applies to a private Alberta limited partnership solely by virtue of its form. An audit may be required by the partnership agreement, financing documents, investors, securities requirements, or applicable tax and regulatory circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No single statutory financial-reporting framework is prescribed for a private Alberta limited partnership. Canadian ASPE or IFRS may be applied according to the partnership agreement, reporting obligations, investor requirements, and applicable Canadian tax-record rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not generally require an annual beneficial-ownership confirmation filing for a limited partnership. The partnership should review beneficial ownership, limited-partner interests, transfers, and control annually; update internal records and file any required registry amendment promptly after a registrable change. Applicable anti-money-laundering, tax, banking, and contractual disclosure obligations remain separate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Declaration of Limited Partnership and all filed amendments
Register of General Partners and Limited Partners
Record of partnership interests, transfers, and beneficial ownership information
Minute book or written resolutions for material partnership decisions
Accounting records and supporting tax documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300-1,200 annually for Alberta registered-office, records, and agent-for-service support, depending on provider and service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 where no audit is required; approximately USD 5,000-25,000 if a voluntary, lender-required, or investor-required certified audit is commissioned
